events.title: Texas governor-elect Hinojosa called for a statewide data center moratorium as a state senator filed a bill to limit cooling methods and require water reporting.
Walmart beat revenue forecasts at $188.8B with e-commerce up 17% and raised its yearly outlook for a third time, though US growth slowed.
Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut and closed at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price, valuing the company near $1.76T.
SpaceX completed a $32B debt sale backed by AI chips, with most of it priced at yields above 8%, high for an investment-grade borrower.
AMD fell 7.7% to about $489 after short seller Hunterbrook alleged its firmware kept reaching a blacklisted Chinese server maker; AMD disputed the claims.
Nvidia fell another 3.3% to about $146 as concerns over its CEO transition and tighter chip export rules outweighed strong quarterly results.
The Dow fell 1,101 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each dropped over 2%, a sixth straight S&P loss, on AI spending doubts and Fed hike fears.
Salt Lake City approved a six-month pause on data centers to write energy and water rules after a $105M project applied for permits.
Jacksonville's city council took up a proposed one-year moratorium on large data center construction.
Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 for the week to Nov 14, slightly above forecasts, with continuing claims at 1.76 million.
Musk said Tesla and SpaceX would probably be better together, as reports point to a possible merger announcement as soon as December.
Anthropic priced its upsized IPO at $83 a share, above its range, raising about $81.3B in the largest offering on record; ANT trades from Nov 19.
Nvidia closed 2.9% lower at about $151 despite beating forecasts, as CEO succession and China risk weighed; AMD rose 5.3% and Broadcom 3.7%.
Neocloud shares including CoreWeave and Iren fell alongside Nvidia after its results failed to lift sentiment.
Minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December and a couple saw room for a larger move.
Target posted 5.6% comparable sales growth, its best in five years, raised its full-year sales outlook and its shares rose about 7%.
Lowe's beat profit forecasts with comparable sales up 1.8%, helped by about $250M of tariff refunds, and trimmed its margin outlook.
Fed Governor Waller said he backs a December hike and could support a half-point move if inflation keeps accelerating.
Nvidia clarified the limits on its future financing support for neocloud customers after Jensen Huang's exit raised doubts about its backstops.
Anthropic is reportedly telling investors its IPO will price at the top of the $70 to $78 range or higher, ahead of Nov 18 pricing.
Home Depot beat sales forecasts with comparable sales up 2.2%, nudged up its profit outlook and named a new CEO, but shares slid over 3%.
UnitedHealth shares fell about 4.7% on renewed concern over Medicare Advantage payments and rising medical use.
Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8B, up 103% on the year, and guided to $130B next quarter with gross margin easing to 71-72% and no China data-center sales assumed.
October retail sales rose 0.2%, slowing from 0.8% in September, as car dealer sales fell 1.6% while online sales rose 1.2%.
Effingham County, Georgia approved the site plan for OpenAI's $20B Project Camellia data center and tabled a data-center moratorium until January.

nvidia.news: Nvidia fell another 3.3% to about $146 on Nov 19, a third straight drop after beating forecasts with $115.8B of revenue (Nov 17), as CEO succession and tighter chip export rules weighed. It also set limits on future neocloud financing (Nov 18).

labs.news: Anthropic opened at $111.50 in its Nasdaq debut and closed at $97.17, up 17% on the $83 IPO price and valued near $1.76T (Nov 19), even as the Dow fell 1,101 points. OpenAI's 457 MW TensorWave deal (Nov 16) adds AMD capacity.
pros: ANT closed 17% above its $83 IPO price
cons: ~$1.76T valuation leaves little room for error
Debut came amid a broad AI sell-off
labs.weak: Anthropic's rich valuation depends on AI spending holding up while the rest of the AI trade is falling.

bigtech.news: The Dow fell 1,101 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq over 2% on Nov 19, a sixth straight S&P loss, on doubts that AI capex will pay off and Fed hike fears; the 10-year yield is 5.07%. Combined 2026 capex guidance stays near $730B.

cloud.news: Nvidia set limits on financing neoclouds (Nov 18) after Huang's exit, and the high-yield spread widened to 3.52% (+0.19 in 30 days). ERCOT demand is up 2.1% and PJM 1.5% on the year; Dallas, TX is 100% in the most severe drought of the hubs, and Prince William and Loudoun in Northern Virginia are 100% and 99.8% in drought.

citizens.news: Salt Lake City paused data centers for six months (Nov 19), Jacksonville weighed a one-year moratorium and Texas' governor-elect called for a statewide one (Nov 20). Household electricity prices are up 5.4% and energy 21% on the year; Dallas, TX is 100% in the most severe drought of the hubs, and Prince William and Loudoun in Northern Virginia are 100% and 99.8% in drought. The saving rate is 3.8%.

spacex.news: SpaceX completed a $32B AI-chip-backed debt sale at yields above 8% (Nov 19) to fund xAI compute, and Musk said a Tesla tie-up would probably make sense. Gas is $3.10, ERCOT demand is up 2.1% and Dallas County is 100% in drought.

tesla.news: Musk said Tesla and SpaceX would probably be better together (Nov 19), with a merger possibly announced in December. Vehicle sales are flat at a 16.0M rate and October car dealer sales fell 1.6%.

consumer.news: No notable Apple news this week. Consumer sentiment is 48.1, down 13% on the year, tech shares fell over 2% on Nov 19, and a December rate hike is expected.

retail.news: Walmart beat with e-commerce up 17% and raised its outlook (Nov 19) after Target's 5.6% comps (Nov 18); retail sales are up 6.8% on the year but rose only 0.2% in October. Temu owner PDD beat profit forecasts (Nov 19).

autos.news: Car dealer sales fell 1.6% in October (Nov 17); vehicle sales are flat at 16.0M and used car prices down 3.3% on the year. The mortgage rate jumped to 7.28% and a December hike would lift loan costs.

fashion.news: Clothing purchases slowed in October (Nov 17); apparel prices are up 3.5% and imports from Vietnam up 61% on the year.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loans stand near $1.78T in the latest (dated) data and higher rates raise borrowing costs.

banks.news: BBB spreads are 1.17% (+0.09 in 30 days), a one-year high, and high-yield 3.52% (+0.19); banks keep pulling back from AI loans and Fed minutes (Nov 18) flagged bank links to private lenders. Goldman and Apollo ran SpaceX's $32B chip debt sale (Nov 19).

fed.news: Target range is 3.75-4.00% with fed funds at 3.88%; core PCE is 3.1% against the 2% goal, unemployment 4.1% and the mortgage rate 7.28%. Waller backed a December hike and left room for a half point (Nov 18); jobless claims rose to 203,000 (Nov 19).

chips.news: AMD fell 7.7% to about $489 on Nov 19 after a Hunterbrook short report alleged its firmware reached a blacklisted Chinese server maker, which AMD disputes; chip stocks gave up early gains as export rules tighten.
pros: Labs keep signing AMD capacity deals
Nvidia guidance implies more TSMC wafers
cons: AMD short report alleges China exposure
chips.weak: Export-control scrutiny now extends beyond Nvidia to AMD.

power.news: No new power deals this week. Gas is $3.10 (-0.12 in 30 days) and grid demand is up 1.5% in PJM and 2.1% in ERCOT on the year, while local moratoriums spread (Nov 19-20).

healthco.news: UnitedHealth fell about 4.7% on Medicare Advantage concerns (Nov 17), while Lilly continues to ride its obesity drugs and its Calytrix deal. Medical care prices are up 1.9% on the year.

industrials.news: No notable news on Boeing, Caterpillar or Lockheed Martin; the Philadelphia Fed factory index fell to 6.3 from 20.9 (Nov 19) and the freight index is down 3.0% on the year.

payments.news: Strong Walmart and Target results (Nov 18-19) point to steady card volumes. Consumer credit is up 3.0% on the year and card delinquency 2.85%.

trade.news: China kept its 24% tariff pause to Jan 10 and the $60B tariff-cut package is still unfinished after Shenzhen meetings (Nov 18-19). Imports from China are up 34%, Mexico 40% and Vietnam 61% on the year.
